name: TixFox – Sell Event Tickets
author: TixFox

sections.description:
TixFox provides a seamless way to sell event tickets directly from your WordPress site. With the block editor integration, you can easily add customizable ticket purchase buttons and full event embeds to your posts and pages.

Key Features

  • Event Button Block: Add customizable “Buy Tickets” buttons with cart icons, custom colors, and styles
  • Event Embed Block: Embed complete event details and ticket purchasing forms via iframe
  • Block Editor Integration: Simple drag-and-drop interface in the WordPress block editor
  • Customizable Appearance: Adjust colors, button sizes, border radius, and icon visibility
  • Modal-Based Purchasing: Smooth modal experience for ticket purchases on button click
  • Event Management: Browse and select from live, upcoming, and past events
  • Modern Design: Clean, responsive blocks that match your site’s aesthetic
  • UTM Parameter Support: Automatic tracking parameter pass-through for analytics

How It Works

  1. Connect your TixFox account via API key in Settings → TixFox
  2. Add TixFox blocks to any post or page using the block editor
  3. Select an event from your TixFox account
  4. Customize the appearance (colors, size, icons)
  5. Visitors can purchase tickets directly from your site

External Services

This plugin connects to the external TixFox API (https://tixfox.co) to function. Here’s how it’s used:

  • Service Used: TixFox
  • API Endpoint Base: https://api.tixfox.co/api/
  • Embed URL Base: https://tixfox.co/embed/e/
  • Purpose: The TixFox API is used to:
    • Fetch your events to select from within the block editor
    • Verify your API key for authentication
    • Display event details and ticket purchasing interface on the frontend
  • Data Sent:
    • API Key: Your TixFox API key (obtained from tixfox.co) is sent with API requests for authentication
    • Event Selection: When selecting events in the editor, event data is fetched from the API
    • UTM Parameters: Marketing tracking parameters from the page URL are automatically passed to the TixFox embed
  • Frequency: API calls occur when:
    • Loading the block editor for TixFox blocks (fetching events list)
    • Loading the plugin settings page (verifying API key)
    • Rendering TixFox blocks on the frontend (loading event embed iframes)
  • Terms and Privacy: Use of the TixFox service is subject to their Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.
    • Terms of Service: https://tixfox.co/terms
    • Privacy Policy: https://tixfox.co/privacy

An active TixFox account and API key are required for this plugin to fetch event data and enable ticket purchasing.

By using this plugin, you agree to the terms and privacy policy of TixFox. A TixFox account and API key are required for the plugin to function.

Third Party Services Tracking

This plugin does not track any user data or include any tracking mechanisms. All event and ticket data is managed through your TixFox account.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the tixfox folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress
  3. Navigate to Settings → TixFox
  4. Create a TixFox account at TixFox.co if you don’t have one
  5. Enter your API key from TixFox.co in the settings page
  6. Add the “TixFox Event Button” or “TixFox Event Embed” block to any post or page
  7. Select an existing event from your account
  8. Customize the appearance and save
sections.faq:
Do I need a TixFox account?

Yes, you need to create an account at TixFox.co to get an API key and manage your events.

Is there a limit to how many ticket buttons I can create?

No, you can create as many ticket buttons and embeds as you need on your WordPress site.

Can I customize the appearance of the buttons?

Yes, you can change button colors, adjust sizes, modify border radius, and choose whether to display the cart icon alongside button text.

What WordPress version is required?

TixFox requires WordPress 5.8 or higher and PHP 7.4 or higher.

Does it work with the block editor?

Yes, TixFox is built specifically for the WordPress block editor (Gutenberg) and provides native block components.

How does the ticket purchasing work?

For the Event Button block, clicking the button opens a modal with the TixFox ticket purchasing interface. For the Event Embed block, the purchasing interface is embedded directly on the page via iframe.
